parties:
Jamuna Knitting and Dying Ltd. and another ----- Appellants (in both the cases)
Vs.
Messer's Y.K. Co. Textile Ltd and others ----- Respondents (in both the cases)
full_judgment: "The learned Counsel appearing for petitioners in the petitioners submits that the present cases involve important question of law including interpretation of several Articles of the Constitution, which are of great public importance, likely to have immense impact on the nation and the society as a whole, that the learned Judges grossly erred in law in holding that Muslim Personal Law of Pre-emption as unconstitutional and offends the provisions of Article 42 of the Constitution, in the face of the fact that section 96(11) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (Act No. XXVIII of 1951), which is a protected law by the first Schedule (under Article 47) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and completely turning blind eye to a decision of the Appellate Division in the case reported in 33DLR (AD) 359, This error has vitiated the whole decision and has resulted serious miscarriage of justice, that the learned Judges also erred in opining that the Muslim Law of Pre-emption offends Articles 31 of the Constitution.
